title: A recipe changed after a meal was logged from it: asked once for a recent meal, older meals keep their foods
why: Coach Milan 23 November 2026, 19:03, after making a recipe (Lazy Burek): he cooked and logged it, then changed the recipe (feta in place of one quark pack, sesame and oil added). The recipe reads PD 4.9 a portion; the meal he ate, under Your cooks, still holds the first foods and PD 6.2. Meaning to agree: is the eaten meal changed with the recipe, or asked. 19:11: think it through; a change could be a correction or a new variation, and a recipe changes again. Proposed 19:12 and agreed (makes sense): every logged meal keeps its own foods; saving a change to a recipe asks once about a meal logged from it today or yesterday, Was it made this way? Update it (same portion share) or Keep it; older meals are not asked, the save says how many keep their foods; Save as a new recipe beside Save for a big change; no warning sign that waits for a stable recipe. 19:35: draw. 20:02 to 20:03: once for all; Go.

opportunity.from: Coach Milan's own recipe, Lazy Burek, 23 November 2026.
opportunity.job: Fix a recipe after cooking it, and have the meal I ate tell the truth.
opportunity.kind: Says something not true: the meal I ate keeps the recipe's first foods after I fix the recipe, with no word.
opportunity.why_now: Recipes are fixed right after the first cook, when the mistake shows.

story: When I change a recipe I already ate from, I want to say whether that meal was made this way, so that my day counts what I really ate and older meals stay as they were.
proposed: 1. Every logged meal keeps its own foods, as now: that record is what was eaten. 2. Save changes on a recipe, when its foods changed and a meal from it was logged today or yesterday, asks once in place: Monday dinner, 18:00, was made from this recipe. Was it made this way? Update it gives the meal the recipe's new foods at the same share it had of the recipe; Keep it as it was leaves it. One line after says which. 3. Older meals are not asked about; one line says how many keep their foods. 4. Save as a new recipe, beside Save changes, for a change that makes a different dish: the recipe stays as it is. The same on the Plate's Update my recipe, which has Save as a new recipe already.
problem: Changing a recipe never touches a meal logged from it. Fixed right after cooking, the recipe reads PD 4.9 a portion while the meal eaten tonight keeps the first foods and PD 6.2, and nothing says so.
checks: Light: the recipe page's Edit recipe and Save changes, and the Plate's Update my recipe. The unit tests with new ones for the share; the build; a new walkthrough for AC1 to AC6; and past-meal-change, recipe-after and recipe-swap, about 5 minutes. New words on screen, so the German sweep too.
decision: Direction agreed 23 November 19:12; once for all 20:03, Go. Checks Light plus the German sweep, 12 of 12. Built in 0.3.187.
now: Cheese pie, eaten tonight at 18:00 for dinner, a quarter of the recipe. I fix the recipe, 250 g of cream cheese in place of 500, and Save changes. Tonight's dinner keeps 125 g of cream cheese and the old numbers; nothing is asked or said.
looked_at: A warning sign on the meal until the recipe is stable: not chosen (19:12); it leaves numbers open with no end and a coach sees half-confirmed days. Changing every meal of the recipe: not chosen; history would change behind my back. Versions of a recipe: not needed; each meal keeps the foods it was made with.

ac.title: Asked once for a recent meal
ac.text: Given Cheese pie eaten tonight at 18:00 for dinner, when I change its foods and tap Save changes, then it asks in place: Monday dinner, 18:00, was made from this recipe. Was it made this way?, with Update it and Keep it as it was

ac.title: Update it
ac.text: Given the question, when I tap Update it, then the dinner takes the recipe's new foods at the share it had (a quarter: 63 g of 250 g cream cheese), its numbers follow, and one line says Your Monday dinner follows the change

ac.title: Keep it as it was
ac.text: Given the question, when I tap Keep it as it was, then the dinner keeps its foods and numbers, and one line says so; the recipe is saved either way

ac.title: Older meals are not asked
ac.text: Given Cheese pie eaten on Friday, when I change it on Monday and Save changes, then nothing is asked, and one line says 1 meal eaten before keeps its foods

ac.title: Only a change of foods asks
ac.text: Given a change to the steps, the name or the portions alone, when I Save changes, then nothing is asked

ac.title: Save as a new recipe
ac.text: Given Edit recipe, when I tap Save as a new recipe, then a new recipe is saved with the changes, the first one stays as it is, and no meal is asked about

unchanged: A logged meal's own Change it and Delete this meal.
The recipe's numbers follow its foods as you type.
The Plate's Update my recipe and Save as a new recipe.
details: Today or yesterday: from midnight of yesterday on the phone's clock. A meal counts as from the recipe when it carries the recipe's id (Your cooks, Every time you ate it).
The share: the meal's grams over the recipe's grams before the change, the same for every food; each food rounded to the gram.
The pictures are the real app on one scratch build of main, not committed, with the clock on Monday 23 November 2026, 19:00.

Built: src/recipeChange.ts (mealsOf, followed, foodsChanged, whenAll); the recipe page asks in place of Save changes; the Plate's Update my recipe (from Make or from a plan slot) leaves the question for the recipe's page on this phone (chefmealan-recipe-ask). Two or more meals today: asked once for all (Coach Milan 20:03).
short: Recipe changed after a meal from it: asked once for today or yesterday; older meals keep their foods
